articleTitle: Estimation methods for power system harmonic effects on power distribution transformers
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: A method of estimating the composite harmonic current generated by the operation of several nonlinear loads connected to a single power distribution transformer is introduced. The author draws upon the information available from industry and proposes an intuitive expansion of the currently available K-factor calculation. The proposed expansion provides a useful tool in specifying properly designed power distribution transformers for operating in a nonsinusoidal load environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Harmonic caused transformer heating evaluated by a portable PC-controlled meter
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: The need for frequent on-site monitoring of harmonic currents both at electric utility ties to industrial and commercial customers and at transformers has increased. If harmonic metering is part of routine measurements, the meter must be easy to use and give a clear record of the measurement. The ability to store the information directly on a computer disk reduces the time and trouble of keeping paper copies in the field. Harmonic heating effects on transformers and a metering technique that is specifically designed for these purposes using a harmonics meter working with an inexpensive notebook or laptop personal computer are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developing and defining basic SCADA system concepts
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: An attempt is made to develop and define the basic concepts of supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems. A SCADA system is complex, and the investment for the organization is a long-term one. Therefore, an electric utility organization must proceed cautiously and with a logical series of steps to ensure that the most cost-effective system that best meets the utility's needs both now and in the future is procured. These steps are developed and defined in detail. These steps have been applied in many SCADA system procurements and have resulted in successful system installations for each organization.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of measures and costs to mitigate magnetic fields from transmission and distribution lines
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: A study of options that can be taken to reduce levels of magnetic fields from operating transmission and distribution lines is presented. How applying limits to existing transmission and distribution lines would affect Missouri Public Service is assessed. Cost estimates are prepared for line reconstruction to mitigate magnetic fields.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EPR power cables rated 105 degrees C/140 degrees C
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: A cable insulation system based on EPR insulation and EPR-based semiconductive layers was introduced over 25 years ago. The possibility of raising the rating of this system was evaluated. The results show it is completely justifiable to rate the EPR system at 105 degrees C for continuous and 140 degrees C for emergency service. Thermal-oxidative aging data are analyzed, and a comparison with older insulations is given. The behavior of power factor and the AC dielectric strength of cable made with this EPR through multiple cycles and after continuous exposure to the elevated temperatures were measured. Comparisons of the resulting data with measurements made at the current 90 degrees C/130 degrees C temperatures are given. The insulation's physical properties after exposure to the proposed higher temperature and the screen resistivities after cyclic and continuous exposure to current and proposed temperatures were measured. Deformation of the EPR versus temperature and measurement of impulse strength after temperature exposures are discussed. Examples of ampacity increases available, suitability of jacketing materials, and moisture resistance of the EPR system are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neutral-to-ground impulse voltage effects on URD cable
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: Full-scale impulse testing of various cable systems that were carried out under the DSTAR (Distribution System Testing, Application, and Research) program, of which the NRECA Rural Electric Research program has been a participant, is described. The primary objective of this phase of the DSTAR program is to evaluate the neutral performance of various cable types under impulse conditions. It also attempts to evaluate the efficacy of a number of neutral grounding schemes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: Power quality is an increasing concern of electric utilities due to growing consumer use of solid-state devices, including computers and microprocessors, in equipment such as microwave ovens, stereos, TVs, and VCRs. Power quality is generally interpreted to include a broad listing of items, including RMS voltage, harmonics, average outage times, momentary interruptions, line flicker, and other values. Line flicker due to motor starting and loading is reviewed. Equipment for measuring flicker, methods for calculating flicker, and four cases involving motor flicker are also reviewed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of polymer-housed distribution arresters for use on rural electric power systems
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: Users have converted to polymer-housed distribution surge arresters because of concerns over violent porcelain arrester failure. There is a false perception in the industry that polymer arresters are intrinsically fail-safe. It is proposed that there is a lack of understanding of the differences in failure mechanisms between porcelain and polymer arresters. Polymer arresters have unique design requirements to provide the desired reliability improvements. This work suggests criteria for rural electric power system user evaluation of polymer arrester design and performance. Users are encouraged to participate in the standards writing process to facilitate changes beneficial to the industry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A digital computer program for radial distribution system analysis
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: A PC-based computer program for accurate analysis of radial distribution systems is described. Objected-oriented design philosophies are used, and the program takes advantage of data encapsulation and class separation to greatly simplify the software development and upgrading process. The program is a Microsoft Windows 3.1 application, and offers many special features to help the user make sound engineering decisions. The interactive design allows fast and simple experimentation with different solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation, selection and implementation of an AM/FM system
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: The author presents an account of the process a group of 15 electric utilities used to evaluate available AM/FM and recommend the one that would best fit the needs of the group. The section on evaluation of AM/FM systems may be of particular interest to someone who is presently considering installing such a system. Also presented is the experience of one of those electric utilities as it implemented the recommended system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Process to identify rural distribution circuit sections for reconstruction
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: The process used to inspect, evaluate, analyze, and recommend candidate rural distribution circuit sections for reconstruction is addressed. Four criteria are assessed during the inspection to determine the physical condition of each circuit section. The assessed criteria include pole condition, hardware condition, primary conductor condition, and specification conformance. A circuit section severity index is assigned to each circuit section based on the value assigned to each criteria. The circuit section severity index is used to determine the relative physical condition of each circuit section. The circuit section severity indices are then ranked and evaluated in conjunction with outage history information and customer density profiles to identify candidate rural distribution circuit sections for reconstruction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculation of horizontal displacement of conductors under wind loading toward buildings and other supporting structures
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: Wind loadings can be the determining factor in the structural design and location of supporting structures, including the choice of materials, sizes, and configuration. Deflection of structures or supported facilities under wind loading may require increased clearances between conductors or cables, thus affecting the physical design of the structures, as well as requiring increased clearances from buildings and affecting the location of the structures themselves. Both exact methodologies and rules of thumb are presented for calculating horizontal loadings and wind deflections of conductors and cables. Tables give values for common conductors that may be used in determining compliance with the National Electrical Safety Code.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: Some of the basic concepts which are common in the design of all substations are described. A general outline for substation design is provided. Substations and their component systems are described, along with the various bus configurations and types of construction in use today. An overview of substation design and general information for the planning and preparation required to design a substation are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution automation today: separating tools from toys
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: Based on an historical perspective of electrical distribution monitoring and control, the application needs of distribution utilities are investigated, and the features, costs, and benefits of automating distribution application areas are evaluated. Each distribution automation program application must stand on its own economically to be truly beneficial to the electric utility. Furthermore, the fixed cost of a system's head-end controller and the initial communication system must be entirely attributed to the initial application of the system. In order to investigate actual costs, justification of a distribution automation system is determined by the experience of a pilot trial period. An application evaluation procedure for distribution automation programs is presented, and a yearly review of each application area is recommended.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Proposed OSHA operations and maintenance work rules for electric utilities
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: The proposed operation and maintenance work rules contained in the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Section 1910.269 proposal are discussed. A summary of the comments on these work rules for the American Public Power Association (APPA) (comments dated 6/1/89 and 9/29/89) and the Edison Electric Institute (EEI) (comments dated 8/1/90, 2/1/91, and 3/15/91) is provided. The impact of the rules on the electric utility industry is assessed. The scope of this study is limited to those portions of the rules which cover transmission and distribution facilities. It mentions but does not discuss the portions affecting power generation facilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Carrying charges: what you should know about transmission access
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: An overview of the principles and issues at the heart of critically important transmission access and wheeling developments in the electric utility industry is provided. Transmission access and wheeling are defined, and the motivations for their emergence are identified. Basic technical concepts are discussed, and some special complexities are outlined. Various approaches to access and pricing are discussed, and current policy issues are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: [Proceedings] 1993 Rural Electric Power Conference. Papers Presented at the 37th Annual Conference
abstract: A discussion of the multifaceted aspects of electric distribution system reliability is provided. A discussion of the tools utilized to measure reliability is presented, and the organizational aspects of reliability performance are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
